# Config-driven status mapping (map-or-drift, round-trip via rebar-status labels)

## Context / Problem

Status mapping is hardcoded: outbound reads built-in `value_maps.LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` at the
CREATE/UPDATE sites (Scope); inbound inverts built-in `config.jira_to_local_status`, preferring
the `rebar-status:<local>` label hardcoded to `blocked`/`cancelled`. A project lacking a rebar
status has no echo-safe remap; a collapse over other statuses has no label. Status must become
config-driven on the S1 core: **map-or-drift** (never skip); remap/collapse must round-trip via
`rebar-status:`.

## Dependency (prerequisite ticket)

On the S1 mapping core **[rebar:bfe7-0900-c3d1-4141]** (merged to `main`): `mapping_config`
provides `load_mapping_config(root=None)` +
`resolve_for_project(config, project_key, *, builtin) -> MappingLayer` (merges
`builtin ← default ← projects.<KEY>`) with `MappingLayer.status_map` (local→Jira; `SKIP` = drop;
ABSENT = drift). `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` is the `builtin`, so no `[mapping]` ⇒ effective map =
today's default — behaviour and parity unchanged.

## Approach — one FORWARD seam; inbound stays reverse-map-free

Only **outbound (forward)** becomes per-project; inbound needs no reverse map/project key — the
`rebar-status:` label makes every non-built-in status self-describing (see 4).

1. **`config.py` — forward resolution entry point.** Add
   `effective_status_map(project_key, root=None) -> dict[str,str]` = `load_mapping_config` +
   `resolve_for_project(builtin=LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA)`. The literal stays the built-in fallback
   (parity-tested); `mapping_config` imported LAZILY (config.py stays stdlib-only). NO reverse
   resolution added.

2. **Outbound consumers read the resolved map via the `OutboundMapper` Protocol.**
   `outbound_differ` resolves the project key once per ticket (`projects_store.resolve_project`
   already runs) and passes the effective `status_map` (optional; `None`→built-in) into both
   Protocol methods: `map_local_to_remote` (CREATE, differ:543) and, via `compute_update_fields`
   (`outbound_field_diff`:291), `map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE). The `_backend.py` Protocol
   signatures + the two backend wrappers (`jira/backend`, `jira_datacenter/backend`) gain the
   param. Value-map `.get()` sites reached: shared `outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote`
   (UPDATE, Cloud+DC), `outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields` (Cloud CREATE),
   `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (DC CREATE). `acli.transition_issue` is NOT threaded — it receives
   the ALREADY-mapped Jira name and passes it through (no double-map).

3. **Drift = leave Jira as-is, never a per-mutation failure.** Decided ONLY in the mapper: with
   no entry for a local status it **omits the `status` field** (Jira unchanged) + a drift alert,
   replacing today's `.get(status,"To Do")` coerce. `reconcile_helpers.preflight_status_mapping`
   needs NO change: it runs AFTER the mapper (`reconcile.py:485`), so a drifted mutation carries
   no `status` field (its skip-when-no-status branch makes it non-offending) and mapped mutations
   carry the tolerated Jira NAME. Kill-switch untouched.

4. **Generalised `rebar-status:` round-trip (built-in-reverse stamp rule).** Outbound
   (`outbound_labels`): stamp `rebar-status:<local>` **iff
   `config.jira_to_local_status.get(status_map[local]) != local`** (`.get`, no KeyError). On the
   built-in map this selects exactly {blocked, cancelled} (in_progress/closed are canonical
   preimages; `deleted` excluded via `excluded_statuses={archived,deleted}`) — default stamping
   preserved. Under ANY config remap/collapse, every status whose Jira target isn't the built-in
   canonical name for `<local>` is labelled → inbound recovers it from the label, no reverse map;
   a DRIFTED status has no target → no label. Inbound: parse the `rebar-status:<local>` suffix,
   validating `<local>` against the local-status vocabulary (a constant — no config/project key),
   via one shared helper; the plain `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS.get()` built-in fallback stays correct
   since every non-built-in status is labelled. Malformed `[mapping]` fails closed via S1's
   `MappingConfigError`.

5. **Fetcher known-set widened.** `fetcher._known_jira_statuses` today reads only built-in
   `config.jira_to_local_status` keys → a config-only status trips a spurious "no reconciler
   mapping" warning. Widen it to built-in ∪ every Jira status NAME declared across config
   (`status_map` values + declared `statuses`, from `repo_root`); kill-switch kept. A superset
   for warning suppression, no per-project threading.

## Scope (files)

- `config.py` — `effective_status_map` (forward only, lazy `mapping_config`).
- `outbound_differ.py` — resolve project key once; pass `status_map` to CREATE/UPDATE Protocol calls + label diff.
- `outbound_field_diff.py` — `compute_update_fields` forwards `status_map` to `map_fields_to_remote`.
- `_backend.py` — `OutboundMapper` Protocol: optional `status_map` on both map methods.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — both wrappers forward `status_map`; DC `_map_local_to_dc_fields` uses it (DC CREATE) w/ fallback + drift-omit.
- `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py` — `map_fields_to_remote` uses `status_map` (UPDATE); drift-omit; fallback.
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — `_map_local_to_jira_fields` uses `status_map` (Cloud CREATE); drift-omit.
- `outbound_labels.py` — stamp rule keyed on built-in `config.jira_to_local_status`.
- `inbound_fields.py` — generalised `rebar-status:<local>` recovery (shared helper); plain built-in reverse unchanged.
- `inbound_translate.py` / `apply_inbound_events.py` / `inbound_differ.py` — use shared helper (retire `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`).
- `applier.py` — re-export shared helper in `__all__`.
- `fetcher.py` — widen `_known_jira_statuses` to built-in ∪ config-declared Jira status names.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` (new).

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit** — pure over the resolved map; tests hit REAL entry points
(`config.effective_status_map`, the outbound mappers, `_diff_status_annotation_labels`,
`inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields`, `fetcher._known_jira_statuses`), never copies. Each
AC below names its test: config-effect, drift (omitted `status` + stderr, not crash/coerce),
remap+collapse round-trip through every inbound site, fetcher no-false-alarm, and the
`value_maps`↔`config` parity guard. Drift alert = a non-fatal stderr line from the mapper (no new
subsystem), asserted via `capsys`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Effective forward map = `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>` via S1
  `resolve_for_project`; a non-default overlay changes the outbound target through the real
  mapper path — `test_status_config_effect`.
- [ ] An unmapped status **drifts**: the mutation omits `status` (Jira unchanged) + a non-fatal
  warning; never skipped nor a per-mutation failure — `test_unmapped_status_drifts`.
- [ ] A config remap AND a collapsed pair (OTHER than blocked/cancelled) round-trip losslessly
  via `rebar-status:<local>` labels, recovered inbound without a reverse map —
  `test_status_remap_roundtrip`/`test_status_collapse_roundtrip`.
- [ ] A config-only Jira status name is known to the fetcher (no spurious warning) —
  `test_fetcher_known_includes_config`.
- [ ] The duplicated `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` literal is retired: each inbound entry point
  (`inbound_fields`/`inbound_translate`/`apply_inbound_events`/`inbound_differ`) recovers a
  generalised label for a local OTHER than blocked/cancelled via the shared helper (the old
  literal could not) — `test_status_label_helper_single_source`.
- [ ] `value_maps`↔`config` parity tests in `state/test_config.py` stay green.
